findings:
The third revision fixes all ten problems from the second review, including the blocking one: the Hacker Frigate now accelerates fast enough to slip out of the player's aim and flight path in time. An independent re-simulation of its movement matches the plan's numbers, and the "do nothing" controls fail as intended. The task order, dependencies and each task's plan sections check out. Five small issues are left, all inside test details or a title. I would approve and let the builders fix them in place. The first two should ideally be patched into the plan text before the Hacker movement task starts.

| # | Severity | Problem | Fix | Tasks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | minor | In Assault, the re-snap 3.5 s later in the slow near-way case pushes the Hacker about 17 px past the view margin. The row's own "view clamp never binds" check is then red, and the run nears the 9 s engagement budget. | Re-snap 1.0 s after the first exit in Assault (or only in Open Space), give the test instance a long engagement budget, and correct the "≤ 75°" text. | t8 |
| N2 | minor | The route-row warm-up does not say whether the player is moving. If it is, no steady orbit exists and the control clears the bound by only 3 ticks. | Say the player is still during the warm-up and starts moving at the snap. Correct the control figures to 3.88 / 2.33 s (nose) and 3.32 / 2.00 s (route). | t8 |
| N3 | minor | A jammer has no brain, so its EMP countdown never runs, and its static overlay and "disrupted" state never end, even after its field lights again. | Derive the jammer's disrupted state and overlay from the field's own suppression timer, and add a row checking both are off 5 s after the Blast. | t7 |
| N4 | minor | The ±1 px range rows (869 / 871, 649 / 651 px) never say how the distance is held: the Hacker and the rockets move several pixels per tick. | Re-place a still player stub and a speed-0 rocket at the exact distance before each tick, or assert only on the tick the cooldown expires. | t9, t10 |
| N5 | minor | The level-1 placement task's title says the jammer comes first, but the default plan sends the Hacker first. | Make the title order-neutral. | t14 |

### N1
At 0.18 rad/s the near-way case re-snaps to about 96° from straight up (anchor at 100°), which is outside `grow(-60)` of the Assault view. The simulated runs take 8.0–8.4 s against the 9.0 s Assault engagement budget. A re-snap 1.0 s after the first exit simulates to a 74.5° maximum.

### N2
At 0.30 rad/s and 720 px, an orbit around a player moving at 100 px/s needs about 238 px/s, above the 230 px/s cap. With a moving warm-up the wrong-way time is 0.43–0.45 s against the 0.5 s limit, and a 3.0 s warm-up fails both rows. A still player during the warm-up reproduces the plan's 1.33 s worst case. The plan's control figures (4.12 / 2.57 s) are about 0.24 s too high, which leaves only 0.13 s of real margin at 720 px.

### N3
`BaseEnemy._physics_process` returns before any EMP clock when there is no brain. Add `HazardField.is_suppressed()` and read it from the jammer's `is_emp_disrupted()` and from its `EmpStatic` overlay visibility.

### N4
From 871 px the Hacker closes to inside the range in about 4 ticks, and a rocket moves about 8.3 px per tick, so a 1 px boundary row is not reproducible as written.

### N5
Cosmetic: option A in the level-1 placement section (the default) sends the Hacker in the 40–53 s window first.

Full evidence, including the re-simulation table, is in `4-review.md` under *Round 3*.
